deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous folio works with theta series attached to a cyclic covering, with roots of unity alpha^g, a primitive root g, and indices kappa+mu. This page studies a theta-type series whose quadratic form pairs the variable n_k with n_{k+mu}:
  Theta(b;v) = sum_{n in Z^{2mu}} exp( (2/pi) sum_{k=1}^{mu} b_k n_k n_{k+mu} + (2/pi) sum_{k=1}^{2mu} v_k n_k ).
The normalising letter is read as pi; it could also be lambda, as on the previous page. The problem is the transformation of this series under the two elementary moves of the modular group, and then under an arbitrary product of them. The product is organised by a continued fraction.

(1) Translation. 'For b_k one may put b_k + g_k g_{k+mu} pi i' (integers g). The extra term is e^{(2/pi) g g' pi i n n'}, which is the periodicity in b. Riemann writes the linear coefficients as v_k = u_{k+mu} b_k, so the series becomes sum exp((2/pi) sum b_k (n_k+u_k)(n_{k+mu}+u_{k+mu})), up to a factor independent of n.

(2) Inversion. This is Poisson summation over each pair (n_k, n_{k+mu}). The two-dimensional Fourier transform of e^{2b x y} is, up to normalisation, (pi/sqrt(-b^2)) e^{2 pi^2 xi eta / b}. This gives
  sum exp((2/pi) sum b_k (n_k+u_k)(n_{k+mu}+u_{k+mu})) = [sqrt(pi) pi^mu / Prod(-b_k)] * sum exp((2/pi) sum (pi^2/b_k) n_k n_{k+mu} + (2/pi) sum pi i u_k n_k).
So b goes to pi^2/b, and the shifts u become characteristics (phases).

(3) Specialisation. Put b_k = pi i tau_{k+k'} c_k. Here tau_k = alpha^{g^k} - alpha^{-g^k} is a cyclotomic (sine-type) quantity, with tau_k = -tau_{k+mu} and c_k = -c_{k+mu}. Inversion then sends c_k to 1/c_k, at least in Riemann's bookkeeping. The prefactor is written 1/(+-Prod c_k), using Prod(-i tau_{k+k'}) = +-sqrt(pi) (later: epsilon = +-1 = Prod(-i tau)/sqrt(pi)). Translation allows 1/c_k -> 1/c_k + m_k with m_k = -m_{k+mu}.

(4) Iteration as a continued fraction. Define p^{nu+1} = m^nu p^nu + p^{nu-1}, with c at stage nu equal to p^nu / p^{nu-1}, and put u_k = v_k / p^nu_k. From the antisymmetry one gets p^nu_{k+mu} = (-1)^nu p^nu_k. The series at stage nu is
  A_nu = sum exp((1/pi) sum_{1}^{2mu} pi i tau_{k+k'} [ (p^{nu+1}/p^nu) n_k n_{k+mu} + 2 v_k n_k / p^nu ]) / (+-Prod p^nu_k).
Completing the square in passing from one stage to the next gives
  A_nu = A_{nu-1} exp((1/pi) sum pi i tau v_k v_{k+mu} / (p^{nu-1}_k p^nu_{k+mu})).

(5) Telescoping. Write p^nu = alpha^nu p + beta^nu q, with p = p^0 and q = p^1. Then alpha^0 = 1, beta^0 = 0, alpha^1 = 0, beta^1 = 1, and both alpha and beta obey the same recursion as p. Parity: alpha^nu_{k+mu} = (-1)^nu alpha^nu_k and beta^nu_{k+mu} = (-1)^{nu+1} beta^nu_k.
- Determinant: alpha^{nu-1} beta^nu - alpha^nu beta^{nu-1} = (-1)^{nu-1}.
- Hence alpha^{nu-1}p/p^{nu-1} - alpha^nu p/p^nu = (alpha^{nu-1}beta^nu - alpha^nu beta^{nu-1}) p q / (p^nu p^{nu-1}).
- Hence (-1)^nu p q/(p^nu p^{nu-1}) = alpha^nu p/p^nu - alpha^{nu-1} p/p^{nu-1} = beta^{nu-1} q/p^{nu-1} - beta^nu q/p^nu.
The step factor is therefore a difference of the quantity beta^nu q/p^nu between consecutive stages. Riemann concludes that
  sum exp((1/pi) sum pi i (tau_{k+k'}/p^nu_k)(p^{nu+1}_k n_k n_{k+mu} + 2 v_k n_k + (beta^nu_k/p_k) v_k v_{k+mu})) * epsilon^nu / (+-Prod p^nu_k)
is independent of nu. This is the theta transformation formula for an arbitrary product of translations and inversions, i.e. a general unimodular substitution.

(6) Closing remarks.
- Replace tau_{k+k'} by tau_k epsilon_k, where epsilon(alpha) is a function of the root of unity with epsilon_k = epsilon_{k+mu}.
- Two Moebius images (p gamma + q delta)/(p alpha + q beta) appear.
- The identity Q_k P'_{k+mu} + Q'_{k+mu} P_k = q_k p'_{k+mu} + q'_{k+mu} p_k expresses invariance of the (sign-twisted) bilinear pairing under a determinant-one substitution.
errors: Convergence: the quadratic form sum b_k n_k n_{k+mu} is indefinite in each pair (n, n'). The series as written cannot converge absolutely for independent integer n_k, n_{k+mu}, so the Poisson-summation step is formal unless the form is really positive in combination with the k' shift. The page does not address this.

In the inversion, pi^2/b with b = pi i tau c gives -pi i/(tau c), not pi i tau (1/c). Riemann's version tacitly needs a relation like tau^2 = -1 or the k <-> k' index juggling (tau_{k+k'} vs tau_{k+mu+k'}), which is not shown. The prefactor sqrt(pi) pi^mu/Prod(-b_k) is likewise loosely normalised (the product presumably runs over 2mu indices under a square root).

The step formula A_nu = A_{nu-1} exp(...) carries 1/pi with sum to 2mu in one line and 2/pi with sum to mu in the next. This is consistent given the k <-> k+mu symmetry and the sign p^nu_{k+mu} = (-1)^nu p^nu_k, but the factor (-1)^nu is absorbed silently.
The continued-fraction algebra (determinant (-1)^{nu-1}, the difference identity, the parity rules) checks out exactly.

results.what: Two-variable Poisson summation for exp(2b(n+u)(n'+u')), giving b -> pi^2/b with shifts turned into characteristics
results.modern_name: Theta inversion formula (Poisson summation; theta transformation under S)

results.what: Composing translations b -> b + m pi i and inversions through a continued fraction p^{nu+1} = m p^nu + p^{nu-1}, with telescoping of the quadratic-completion factors via the determinant identity, giving the transformation of theta under a general unimodular substitution (invariant independent of nu)
results.modern_name: Theta transformation under SL2(Z) via generators / continued fractions; related to the continued-fraction evaluation of Gauss sums
results.usually_credited_to: Hermite (1858) for the general theta transformation; continued-fraction Gauss-sum methods (Genocchi, Kronecker, later Landsberg/Krazer)

results.what: Applying this to theta series with cyclotomic coefficients tau_k = alpha^{g^k} - alpha^{-g^k} attached to cyclic coverings, with an epsilon(alpha) twist and the sign product epsilon = Prod(-i tau)/sqrt(pi)
results.modern_name: Theta transformations for abelian varieties with cyclotomic (complex/real) multiplication
results.usually_credited_to: unsure (later work on Jacobians of cyclic/Fermat curves)

results.what: Invariance of q p' + q' p (sign-twisted) under determinant-one substitutions
results.modern_name: Invariance of the symplectic/bilinear pairing under SL2

deep.surprise_reason: The core technique (theta inversion plus translations composed through a continued fraction, with telescoping via the convergent determinant) is classical for Riemann's time (Jacobi, Hermite 1858) and routine in content. The mildly interesting feature is applying it to theta series of cyclic coverings with cyclotomic coefficients, but the page is fragmentary and formal (convergence ignored), so it does not establish a new result.

Line 3: 'tau_k = alpha^{g^k} g_{k+mu} + Ind.2' is uncertain. It probably records a congruence or index condition mod 2 on tau_k or its index, not an equation.
'c_k u_k = v/p^{nu-1}' has a struck-out superscript (nu+1). The intended relations are u_k = v_k/p^nu_k and c_k u_k = v_k/p^{nu-1}_k.
Final German remark reads approximately: 'Für tau_{k+k'} zu setzen tau_k epsilon_k, wo epsilon(alpha) eine [ganze?] Function [ist], für welche epsilon_k = epsilon_{k+mu}'.
The sign (+-) in front of Prod p^nu_k is written as a boxed or struck +-, consistent with an undetermined sign epsilon^nu.
